haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go only to the shadow store, which is the new engine's store in shadow mode.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store, with no charges.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person asks the controller to move it forward.
haiku-low.q4: A person starting a manual rollback, or the controller automatically when the new engine's charge failure rate exceeds 2% over 10 minutes. Automatic starts happen only in both or new_only.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with gate counters reset. The new engine must go through shadow again and meet Gate A and Gate B with Finance sign-off.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback stops being possible on day 35 after new_only was entered. The usage log keeps events only 35 days, so skipped events could be lost.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence is kept in the rollout record. The controller, the only writer of billing_mode, rejects any move unless the gate is met and a person asked.
haiku-low.q9: The rollout controller detects it by measuring the new engine's charge failure rate from provider responses over any 10-minute window. When above 2%, it starts a rollback and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: New-engine charging is frozen, so nothing is queued and due periods are found again at reconcile. The old engine charges them after the flip to old_only.
haiku-low.q11: A charge key, one per customer and billing period, used at ledger and provider. Pending entries are written under it, and settle never re-charges until the provider says not charged.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays at that step with charging frozen and the mode unchanged. The step is retried and on-call is paged, and the mode flips only after reconcile stores its list.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store only.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and does not charge.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared (read as a 7-day total, to be confirmed). A person asks the rollout controller, which accepts only one step forward and only from a person.
sonnet.q4: The rollout controller starts it automatically when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. This happens only in `both` or `new_only`, and it also pages on-call. Errors in `shadow` never start a rollback, and from day 35 on in `new_only` there is no rollback, only a page.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`, with the gate counters, Finance sign-off and charging-frozen flag cleared. The rollout must then go through `shadow` again with every gate counter at zero, meeting gate A (and later gate B plus Finance sign-off) before the new engine takes over.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 after `new_only` was entered, when it becomes `new_only_locked`. The document says only that the brief states there is no way back from day 35 on, and gives no further reason.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED. The document does not say how workers learn of a mode change or what happens to an in-flight invoice. It says only that on the flip the new engine is off and its in-progress work is dropped, and that ledger entries already written stay.
sonnet.q8: The evidence (gate counters, nightly mismatch rate and invoices compared, Finance sign-off) is kept in the rollout record. The controller accepts only one step forward, only from a person and only if the gate is met, and otherwise rejects the request. Skipping a step is rejected.
sonnet.q9: The rollout controller. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate from provider responses: declined or errored charge attempts divided by all new-engine attempts in a 10-minute window. When the rate is above 2% in `both` or `new_only`, it starts the rollback (freeze first) and pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: Charging is frozen and nothing is queued. Periods that come due while frozen are found again at reconcile and put on the list of periods due. After the flip, the old engine charges first the listed periods and then normal runs, so customers may be billed late.
sonnet.q11: The charge key, one idempotency key per customer and billing period, used at the ledger and the payment provider by both engines. Settle also looks up every pending entry at the provider and never re-charges until the provider says it was not charged. Reconcile counts a period as due only if no charged entry exists under its key. The old engine removes a period from the list once it has a charged entry.
sonnet.q12: The rollback stays at the failed step and retries, and pages on-call. Charging stays frozen and the mode does not flip, so customers may be billed late but not twice. The rollout record holds the current step and the starting mode. If the old engine crashes after the flip, it restarts from what is left in the list, and the charge key prevents double charges.
